name: MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox
title: MarketingConsentCheckbox
summary: An opt-in to marketing messages: one checkbox, or one per channel, with its notes, that reports the exact wording shown with every change.
whenToUse: On sign-up, checkout and contact forms that ask for permission to send marketing, and on a settings screen where the person changes that choice.
whenNotToUse: For agreeing to terms or a policy that is required to continue use MonarchCheckboxRow. For an ordinary setting use MonarchSwitchRow.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox(selection: Set<MonarchMarketingChannel>, onConsentChange: (MonarchMarketingConsent) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, channels: List<MonarchMarketingChannel> = listOf(MonarchMarketingChannel.Email), enabled: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, showUnsubscribeNote: Boolean = true, policyTitle: String? = null, onPolicyClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchMarketingConsentCheckboxLabels = MonarchMarketingConsentCheckboxLabels())
enum class MonarchMarketingChannel { Email, Sms, Phone, Post }
class MonarchMarketingConsent(channels: Map<MonarchMarketingChannel, Boolean>, text: String, at: Long) { val granted: Set<MonarchMarketingChannel> }
class MonarchMarketingConsentCheckboxLabels(unsubscribeNote: String? = null, channelLabels: Map<MonarchMarketingChannel, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: selection
options.description: The channels the person agreed to. Start it empty.

options.name: onConsentChange
options.description: Called on every change with each channel's state, the wording shown and the time in epoch milliseconds. Store granted as the new selection and keep the record as proof.

options.name: channels
options.description: The channels to ask about. One checkbox each when there are several.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the choice can be changed and the policy opened.

options.name: label
options.description: The question. Built in: "Send me product news by email" (or by text message, phone, post) for one channel, "Send me product news" for several.

options.name: description
options.description: What is sent and how often.

options.name: showUnsubscribeNote
options.description: Shows "You can unsubscribe at any time."

options.name: policyTitle
options.description: The text of a link to the privacy policy. Shown only with onPolicyClick.

options.name: onPolicyClick
options.description: Opens the privacy policy; the app navigates.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the unsubscribe note and the channel labels.

states.name: one channel
states.description: One checkbox row whose label is the question, with the description and the note as its description.

states.name: several channels
states.description: The question as a heading, the notes, then one checkbox row per channel.

states.name: ticked
states.description: The Material 3 checkbox in the accent color with a check mark.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The checkboxes, the question, the notes and the link use the disabled colors; nothing responds.

appearance: The checkboxes are MonarchCheckboxRow. The question heading uses the default text color, the notes the muted text color and the policy link the link color with an underline; all switch to the disabled text color when disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ignores defaultChecked so the boxes cannot start ticked; here the selection is hoisted, as for every Compose control, so the component cannot enforce it: the documentation tells the app to start it empty. The web posts hidden form inputs (name, textName); a native app has no form post, so the app stores the MonarchMarketingConsent it receives. The wording is built from the strings the component draws. The web takes React nodes and a policy href; here the texts are plain strings and the policy is a title with an onPolicyClick callback, because Monarch components do not navigate. iOS takes a URL for the policy. The time is epoch milliseconds (UTC) instead of an ISO string or a Date.
accessibility: Each checkbox is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the Checkbox role, the label (and, with one channel, the notes), read as checked or not checked; the whole row is the touch target, at least 48dp high.
With several channels the question has the heading property, so it can be reached with heading navigation.
The policy link reserves a touch target of at least 48dp by 48dp, draws the focus ring and is underlined, so it does not depend on color.
When disabled every checkbox and the link are read as disabled and ignore taps.
edgeCases: The same channel listed twice is shown once.
An empty channels list is treated as email.
The wording collapses runs of whitespace, so line breaks in a description do not change the proof text.
The policy title without onPolicyClick is not shown, because it could not be opened.

examples.title: In a contact form
One checkbox per channel
examples.code:
MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox(
    selection = channels,
    onConsentChange = { channels = it.granted },
    channels = listOf(MonarchMarketingChannel.Email, MonarchMarketingChannel.Sms, MonarchMarketingChannel.Post),
)
